title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops & Top Support Issues
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates standards, templates, and canonical fixes for Developer Experience (DevEx) docs: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and top support issues. It exists to: 1) reduce time-to-first-success for new users, 2) keep examples consistent and testable, and 3) provide on-call and support teams with canonical troubleshooting steps.

Scope and goals
- Audience: SDK authors, docs maintainers, solutions engineers, and on-call SREs.
- Includes: Python/Node SDK guides, minimal quickstarts, canonical curl + HTTP examples, templates for docs pages, review & publishing process, and the top support issues with verified fixes.
- Non-goal: detailed model architecture docs (see eng-serving-runtime).

Ownership and contacts
- Doc owner: Developer Experience (eng-developer-experience).
- Primary contact: Jordan Kim (author).
- Reviewers: Priya Rao, Liam O'Connor, Marisol Vega.
- Escalation path: devex-oncall -> eng-infra -> eng-platform (pager: #devex-oncall).

Structure and repository layout
- Source repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/devex-docs.git (branching: main, staging).
- CI: devex-docs-ci (runs lint, link-check, example-tests). Job names: docs/lint, docs/spellcheck, docs/linkcheck, docs/examples-e2e.
- Templates live in: /templates/{sdk-guide,quickstart,api-example,page}. Use the page template to create new guides.

Publishing & release cadence
- Continuous publishing for small fixes (merged to main triggers devex-docs-ci -> docs-site deploy).
- Monthly content roundup on first Monday (content owners: assigned in page metadata).
- Major rework: create a PR, add reviewers, tag with release-notes and schedule rollout.

Review checklist (minimum before publish)
1. Title and intro present and concise.
2. Code examples run in docs/examples-e2e pipeline (pass).
3. No broken internal links (linkcheck < 0.5% broken).
4. Accessibility: images have alt text.
5. Labels and owner_team set.
6. Reviewer approvals: >= 1 engineering reviewer + 1 devex reviewer.

Naming conventions and file format
- Filenames: short, hyphenated, end with YYYY-MM-DD or -vN.json for revisions, e.g., developer-experience-sdk-quickstarts-2026-12-01.json.
- Page metadata required fields: title, space, author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated.
- Content: prefer plain text sections with code fences for snippets; tables for config.

SDK Guides: recommended structure
Each SDK guide should include these sections:
- Quick summary (1–2 lines)
- Install and upgrade commands
- Minimal example (copy/paste runnable)
- Authentication and common error cases
- Advanced patterns (streaming, retries, batching)
- Versioning/deprecation notes
- Tests and CI hooks

Python minimal example
```
# install
pip install redwood-inference-sdk==1.4.0

from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1-small", prompt="Write a short haiku about latency.")
print(resp.text)
```
Notes: pin to a patch version for reproducible quickstarts (1.4.x). Update example in docs/examples/py/minimal.py and ensure docs/examples-e2e runs with matrix: python 3.10, 3.11.

Node minimal example
```
# install
npm install @redwood-inference/sdk@1.4.0

import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })

const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1-small', prompt: 'Summarize serverless in one sentence.' })
console.log(r.text)
```

Authentication & secrets
- Use REDWOOD_API_KEY environment variable in quickstarts.
- For CI: store keys in secrets manager and rotate every 90 days. Deployed docs should never contain live keys.

API Examples (canonical)
- Always include: curl example, Python snippet, Node snippet, and streaming example when applicable.
- Example: text generation (REST)
Curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${REDWOOD_API_KEY}" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Translate to French: Hello world"}'
```
Streaming (server-sent events)
- Use streaming when client latency budget < 300ms per token and client supports SSE/WebSocket.
- Node SSE example included in templates/streaming-example.js.

Errors & canonical responses
- 401: check API key, ensure correct prefix, and check account status.
- 429: apply exponential backoff (initial 200ms, factor 2, max 10s) and surface client-friendly message.
- 5xx: implement retry with jitter and fallback to a lower-cost model variant (see routing policy).

Quickstarts & templates
- Quickstart types: minimal-hello-world, web-chat-demo, embeddings-search-template, function-calling-template.
- To create a quickstart from template:
  1. git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/quickstarts.git && cd quickstarts
  2. cp -r templates/embeddings-search my-embeddings-demo
  3. Update README.md: add setup, env vars, verification steps.

Environment variables (canonical table)
| NAME | DESCRIPTION | DEFAULT | REQUIRED |
| REDWOOD_API_KEY | API key for Redwood | none | yes |
| REDWOOD_MODEL | Model used in quickstart | redwood-1-small | no |
| DEVEX_EXAMPLE_PORT | Local server port | 8080 | no |

Docs site operating procedures (docs-site)
- CI pipeline: PR -> staging (preview deploy) -> approve -> merge to main -> production deploy.
- Preview URL naming: https://docs-preview.redwood.dev/pr-{PR_NUMBER}/path/to/page
- Backfill policy: if a page references a new SDK version, mark as 'versioned' and add note in page footer.
- Analytics: page views and search terms are tracked in docs-analytics (weekly digest).

Service-level KPIs for docs & examples
- docs/examples-e2e pass rate >= 98% on main branch.
- Docs site deploy time (staging->prod) < 10 minutes.
- Broken link rate < 0.5% per week.
- Average time to reviewer approval for docs PRs: <= 48 hours (measured monthly).

Top support issues and canonical fixes
1) Symptom: "401 Unauthorized" in quickstarts and examples.
   - Root cause: malformed or missing REDWOOD_API_KEY, or using a test key on production endpoint.
   - Canonical fix: verify env var, run `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY | sed -n '1p'` (do not print keys in public logs), ensure no leading/trailing whitespace. For CI, confirm secret is mounted in job (CI step: print 'KEY_PRESENT' if length>0).
   - Verification: run `curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/status` -> expect 200.

2) Symptom: "Model mismatch / unexpected output quality" (users hit older pinned model).
   - Root cause: quickstart pinned to older model or mismatch between SDK default and API default.
   - Canonical fix: update quickstart README and examples to use the recommended model (e.g., redwood-1-small or redwood-1-embed-v2). Add a migration note if behavior changed.
   - Verification: run example and compare generation against the approved sample output in docs/examples/golden/*.txt.

3) Symptom: "429 Too Many Requests" from client SDKs.
   - Root cause: no client-side rate limit or sudden burst of parallel requests (e.g., serverless cold-start storm).
   - Canonical fix: implement token-bucket or concurrency limit in quickstart backends. Example JS retry helper included in templates/retry-helper.js (exponential backoff with full jitter).
   - Verification: run load test (k6 script in templates/load-test/k6.js) and observe 429 count == 0 under target RPS.

4) Symptom: "Streaming disconnects / truncated responses".
   - Root cause: proxy timeouts or client not reconnecting properly on transient network errors.
   - Canonical fix: for preview and prod proxies, set idle timeout >= 120s for streaming routes. Update Nginx/ALB config: `proxy_read_timeout 180s;` For clients, implement reconnect + resume logic documented in streaming-example.js.
   - Verification: run streaming e2e test (docs/examples-e2e streaming job) for 10k-char output and confirm full payload received.

5) Symptom: "Tokenization / token count mismatch causing high billing".
   - Root cause: client libraries or user tokenizers differ from Redwood's tokenizer; prompts include hidden characters or large metadata.
   - Canonical fix: add a token-count utility in each quickstart (python and node) and show token estimates before sending. Example: `from redwood.tokenizer import count_tokens; count_tokens(prompt)`. Update docs to recommend trimming long contexts and moving metadata to embeddings index.
   - Verification: run token-count on sample dataset and confirm token counts match server-side token meter within +/- 2 tokens for short inputs.

Post-incident & triage playbook (for doc-related regressions)
1. Declare owner and priority (owner: devex oncall).
2. Reproduce against main branch in staging preview.
3. If fix is content-only -> hotfix PR + reviewer sign-off -> merge -> prod deploy.
4. If fix requires code change (examples runner or SDK) -> follow engineering release process, include rollback plan, and tag docs with 'workaround' until resolved.

Testing and automation guidance
- Examples must be runnable in a hermetic environment. Use the dockerized test runner: devex/examples-runner:stable.
- Golden outputs stored in docs/examples/golden/. CI compares outputs with `diff -u`. If non-deterministic, use fuzz thresholds recorded in test metadata.

Appendix: Useful commands
- Run examples locally: `scripts/run-examples --language python --example minimal`
- Run linkcheck: `make linkcheck`
- Preview build: `make preview` -> visit the preview URL in CI artifact.
- Add label to a page: add `labels` metadata in JSON header and push via docs-edit-bot.

Change log
- 2026-07-12: Created, baseline guide for SDKs and quickstarts.
- 2026-09-01: Added canonical fixes for tokenization mismatches and streaming proxies.
- 2026-12-01: Updated publishing cadence and CI job names; added golden output verification step.

If you are updating or creating a new quickstart, use the page template and follow the Review checklist. For questions or help migrating an example, contact the Developer Experience owners on #devex-docs or open a PR in the repo.
